findings.title: Migration aborts when no embed_category row matches, which is the common case
findings.body: The category lookup `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. The query only matches when site_settings.embed_category holds the name of an existing category. Most installs never set that setting (its default is empty), so the result is empty, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration fails on upgrade. The intended fallback to the uncategorized category (`if category_id == 0`, line 14) can never run: it would need a matched row with id 0, and the crash happens first. The uncategorized lookup on line 15 also indexes `[0]['value']` without checking for rows.

findings.title: Legacy host values are copied without normalization or SQL escaping
findings.body: Values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are inserted verbatim. EmbeddableHost's before_validation strips the scheme and path, and the old allows_embeddable_host? accepted entries like 'https://example.com/1234' (it parsed them with URI). Migrated rows keep those prefixes, so EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, which compares lower(host) to a bare hostname, never matches them. Embeds for those sites silently stop working after upgrade. The value is also interpolated into SQL without escaping, so a host containing an apostrophe aborts the migration. Trailing '\r' from CRLF input is also kept. Normalize each entry (strip scheme, path, whitespace, and '\r') and use bound parameters.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called before validations run. If host is nil (for example, the admin create or update request omits embeddable_host[host]), this raises NoMethodError instead of producing a validation error. The admin controller then returns a 500 rather than a 422. The format validator on line 2 would have rejected nil cleanly, but it never runs. Guard the nil case or add a presence check before normalizing.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation or unique index on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents two rows with the same host, case-insensitively or otherwise. The migration adds no unique index and the model has no validates_uniqueness_of. record_for_host (line 17) calls .first with no ORDER, so if duplicates exist with different categories, the category assigned to imported topics is arbitrary. Add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation and a unique index on lower(host).

findings.title: category_id is never checked against an existing category
findings.body: `belongs_to :category` does not verify that category_id points to a real category, and the table has no foreign key. The admin controller passes through any integer (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb line 24). Deleting a category, or saving a bad id, leaves a host pointing at nothing. TopicEmbed.import then passes that id to PostCreator, so new embed topics get a dangling category. Validate that the category exists.

findings.title: _ids sideloading yields undefined entries and throws on null
findings.body: _hydrateEmbedded now maps every *_ids array through _lookupSubType. If the referenced collection is absent from the payload, _lookupSubType returns undefined for each id, and the result is an array of undefined entries. The `hydrated || []` fallback on line 200 never applies because map always returns an array, so the undefined entries survive. The embedding template then renders a row per entry. Separately, `obj[k].map` throws when the _ids value is null. Previously *_ids keys were ignored entirely, so a single null field now breaks hydration of the whole record. Filter out missing entries and guard null before mapping.

findings.title: Admin CRUD endpoints have no behavioral tests
findings.body: The only spec asserts that the controller subclasses Admin::AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, or destroy; the category default to uncategorized (controller line 25); the response for an unknown id; validation failures; or the staff-only filter. embedding_controller_spec.rb has the same single inheritance assertion. A regression in the endpoints the admin UI depends on would pass CI. Add request specs for each action, including the failure paths.

findings.title: update and destroy crash with 500 for unknown ids
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without a nil check. For a nonexistent or already-deleted id, `host.host =` (line 23) or `host.destroy` (line 16) raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Use find (which raises RecordNotFound) or check for nil and return not_found.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op
findings.body: `update` renders the current embedding without reading params or saving anything, so the endpoint returns success while changing nothing. The client saveChanges action (admin-embedding controller) calls it with update({}), but the template has no save button, so the action is dead and the endpoint is misleading. Either implement the update or remove the route and the client action.

findings.title: record_for_host does not downcase the input before comparing to lower(host)
findings.body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` against the URI host, but the input is never downcased. Any mixed-case host fails to match a stored host. Callers include TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, which passes the raw embed_url param (only TopicEmbed normalizes URLs), so an embed_url with an uppercase host is treated as not embeddable and never retrieved. Downcase the host before the lookup.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
findings.body: The format validator on line 2 explicitly allows an optional :port, and before_validation keeps it. But record_for_host compares against uri.host, which never includes a port. An entry like example.com:8080 is accepted by validation and can never match a referer or embed_url. Either reject ports in validation or compare host and port together.

findings.title: Host validation rejects TLDs longer than five letters
findings.body: The regex requires the TLD to be `[a-z]{2,5}`. That rejects valid hosts such as example.technology, example.community, or example.international, and any host without a dotted TLD such as localhost. This is a new validator on a new table, so it blocks legitimate entries that the old free-text setting accepted.

findings.title: Feed-imported topics lose their category, with no default left to configure
findings.body: Previously every imported post was placed in SiteSetting.embed_category. That setting is removed here (site_settings.yml, server.en.yml, and the migration's DELETE). TopicEmbed.import now takes the category only from a matching EmbeddableHost. import is also reached from feed polling and import_remote, which do no host check. Feed-imported topics whose URL host is not registered silently land in the uncategorized category, and no admin setting remains to define a default. This is a behavior regression that should be called out or handled.

findings.title: Failed host deletion gives no feedback
findings.body: delete() calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no catch. Every other request in this component uses popupAjaxError (see save on line 40). If the delete fails (for example a 403 or 500), the promise rejection is unhandled, the user sees nothing, and the row stays in the list. Add .catch(popupAjaxError).

findings.title: Test named for embeddable host checks behavior that no longer exists
findings.body: expandable_first_post? no longer reads embeddable hosts, so the test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes only because the built topic has no TopicEmbed row (has_topic_embed? is false for an unsaved topic). It does not exercise host presence at all, and no test replaces the old 'hosts disabled' coverage. The nested describe on the following lines is also misspelled ('emeddable').

findings.title: find embedded test changed to id 2, but the fixture always returns fruit 1
findings.body: The test now calls store.find('fruit', 2), but the /fruits/:id pretender route in create-pretender always returns fruits[0] (apple, id 1), ignoring the id. The assertions therefore check apple's colors. Changing the id suggests coverage of the banana record (color_ids [3]) that does not exist. Either make the fixture honor the id or revert the id to 1.

findings.title: Fabricator definitions are swapped between the two files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now defines :embeddable_host, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category, and :private_category fabricators. Fabrication loads every file, so specs still run. But the names are wrong: anyone looking for the category fabricators, or for the host fabricator, will open the wrong file, and the history of category_fabricator.rb is muddled. Swap the contents back so each file matches its name.
